title: Template Inheritance & Reusability
description: Create a base template and extend it to avoid repetition.

slides.title: The DRY Principle in Templates 📚
slides.content:
Most websites have a consistent layout: header, footer, navigation. Instead of copying that HTML into every page, we create a **base template** and **extend** it.

- `{% extends "base.html" %}` – tells Django to use the base template.
- `{% block content %} ... {% endblock %}` – defines areas where child templates can insert content.

slides.title: Base Template (base.html)
slides.content:
My Site

...
{% block content %} {% endblock %}
© 2025

slides.title: Child Template (home.html)

quizData.question: Which template tag is used to define a section that can be overridden by child templates?
quizData.explanation: `{% block %}` defines a placeholder that child templates can fill. `{% extends %}` is used to inherit from a base template.

slides.title: Using `include`
slides.content:
For reusable components that are not layout‑wide, use `{% include "navbar.html" %}`. This inserts the content of another template at that point.

```html
{% include "components/header.html" %}
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `block.super` to preserve parent content

In a child block, you can call `{{ block.super }}` to include the parent block's content and then add your own.
